messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@finsolve.com>, Ken Li <ken.li@finsolve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit - Finsolve

Hi Jordan / Ken —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Wanted to capture the highlights and next steps so we’re aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Unpredictable latency and throttling during market open spikes (daily burst windows).
- High per-token costs from frequent retries and lack of batching for your synchronous inference workloads.
- Security/isolation requirement: must run on customer-dedicated GPUs (no multi-tenant), SOC 2 controls, and customer-managed KMS.
- Need clear audit logs and 30-day retention for query traces for compliance.

Current stack
- Inference clients call an API gateway -> internal autoscaling k8s service (GPU-backed) running Llama-2 family models (quantized).
- Traffic pattern: baseline ~20 rps, peak ~130 rps for 30-45 minutes each market open. Average request size ~1.2k tokens; some batching possible.
- On-prem data & partially cloud hybrid for model storage.

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit
- Predictable throughput: reserved capacity that supports sustained 120 rps and 20k tokens/sec with headroom for 1.5x bursts.
- Latency: median end-to-end <200ms for 1.2k-token requests during baseline, <400ms in peak with graceful degradation.
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pool, customer-managed keys, and network peering (VPC).
- Ops: autoscaling + burst capacity to handle 1.5x-2x spikes without cold-start regressions.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence, 30-day audit log retention, and access controls for model version pinning.

What Redwood can offer (high level)
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with predictable TPS and configured burst windows.
- Autoscaling & burst: configurable policies that prioritize latency SLOs; automatic fallback to smaller variants if capacity constrained.
- Private deployment options: VPC peering and customer KMS integration.
- Observability: per-route latency/cost breakdowns and token-level tracing to help diagnose hotspots.

Open questions / items to size
1) Typical concurrent connections and percent of requests that are synchronous vs async.
2) Maximum acceptable cost per request (ops budget guardrail).
3) Whether you can tolerate model-variant fallbacks for brief periods (e.g., quantized vs full-precision) or require strict model fidelity.
4) Preferred times for technical deep-dive with your infra team (we should include your SRE/infra lead).

Attachments
- redwood-dedicated-one-pager.pdf (high-level features & SLA)
- finsolve-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (starter MAP; editable)

Proposed next steps
- Jordan: share SRE/infra contact + rough concurrency numbers by EOD Tue.
- Rafael/Marissa: schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive to align on sizing (link below).
- Rafael: send updated MAP and preliminary capacity recommendation after deep-dive.

Schedule: https://calendly.com/rafael-redwood/rd-dedicated-demo
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7892

Thanks - looking forward to the next call.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit - Finsolve

Thanks Rafael - this is exactly what I wanted to capture. A few clarifications from our side:

- Concurrency: baseline concurrent requests ~40, peak concurrent ~260 during market open (that maps to the 130 rps number because many requests are long-polling).
- Token distribution: 75% of requests are 500-1.5k tokens; 25% are 3k+ tokens (these are lower frequency but very latency sensitive).
- Cost target: we’re aiming to reduce per-request infra spend by ~30% vs our current setup.
- Model fidelity: for critical flows (risk scoring, trade-sentiment) we need model parity - fallbacks only acceptable for non-critical paths.
- Compliance: procurement will require SOC 2 Type II evidence and our security team needs to review KMS integration before PO.

I’ll loop in procurement and our SRE lead (Ken) to schedule the deep-dive. We can do Tues/Wed next week afternoon PT.

Jordan
VP, Platform Engineering | Finsolve
jordan.blake@finsolve.com
